artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

Split Enz.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
True Colours, released in January 1980, is the sixth studio album by New Zealand band Split Enz, marking a pivotal moment in their career as their first major commercial success. Musically, the album blends rock and pop with strong new wave influences, showcasing a polished sound that balances catchy melodies with inventive arrangements. The record features more prominent contributions from Neil Finn, who emerged as a key songwriter and vocalist alongside Tim Finn, adding fresh energy and depth to the band's evolving style.

The album was originally released on Mushroom Records in Australasia and later on A&M Records internationally, reflecting its broad appeal beyond the band’s home region. Tracks like "I Got You" became signature hits, helping True Colours reach a wider audience and cement Split Enz’s place in the early 1980s pop/rock landscape. Critically, the album is often praised for its sophisticated production and memorable songwriting, and it remains a defining work in Split Enz’s discography, bridging their art-rock roots and more accessible pop sensibilities.
